title: Prakrama 2, Sarga 13. The Brahmana's Curse as a Boon
html:
The Lord and His devotees clean the temple; He refuses to heal a leper who offended Srivasa, but at Srivasa's request promises to save him, and Jagai and Madhai as well; the Lord accepts the curse of an offended brahmana as a blessing to take sannyasa

Verse 1

अथापरदिने देवो भक्तिं संशिक्षयन्स्वकान्।
देवालयं ययौ विप्रैः सार्धं सम्मार्जनीं करे॥१॥

athāparadine devo bhaktiṁ saṁśikṣayansvakān|
devālayaṁ yayau vipraiḥ sārdhaṁ sammārjanīṁ kare||1||

atha — then; apara-dine — on another day; devah — the Lord; bhaktim — devotion; sanshikshayan — teaching; svakan — His own people; deva-alayam — to the temple; yayau — went; vipraih — with brahmanas; sardham — together; sammarjanim — a broom; kare — in the hand.

1On another day the Lord, teaching His own people devotion, took a broom in His hand and went with the brahmanas to the temple.

Verse 2

कुद्दालं चांसभागेषु धटीं कटिवरे वहन्।
नूत्नवस्त्रकृतोष्णीषो बालसूर्यसमप्रभः॥२॥

kuddālaṁ cāṁsabhāgeṣu dhaṭīṁ kaṭivare vahan|
nūtnavastrakṛtoṣṇīṣo bālasūryasamaprabhaḥ||2||

kuddalam — a hoe; cha — and; amsa-bhageshu — on the shoulders; dhatim — a loincloth; kati-vare — on the fine hips; vahan — carrying; nutna-vastra-krita-ushnishah — with a turban made of new cloth; bala-surya-sama-prabhah — radiant like the young sun.

2He carried a hoe on His shoulder and wore a loincloth about His fine hips; a turban of new cloth crowned His head, and He shone like the rising sun.

Verse 3

आचार्याद्या महात्मानः कुद्दालमार्जनीकराः।
कृष्णस्य हड्डिपा भूत्वा द्वारं देवालयस्य ते॥३॥

ācāryādyā mahātmānaḥ kuddālamārjanīkarāḥ|
kṛṣṇasya haḍḍipā bhūtvā dvāraṁ devālayasya te||3||

acharya-adyah — headed by the Acharya; maha-atmanah — the great souls; kuddala-marjani-karah — with hoes and brooms in hand; krishnasya — of Krishna; haddipah — sweepers; bhutva — having become; dvaram — the gate; deva-alayasya — of the temple; te — they.

3The great souls headed by the Acharya, hoes and brooms in hand, became Krishna's sweepers1, and, coming to the gate of the temple,

Verse 4

भित्तिं सम्मार्जयामासुः सह कृष्णेन सद्गुणाः।
एवंप्रकारं नृहरेः शिक्षां शतसहस्रशः॥४॥

bhittiṁ sammārjayāmāsuḥ saha kṛṣṇena sadguṇāḥ|
evaṁprakāraṁ nṛhareḥ śikṣāṁ śatasahasraśaḥ||4||

bhittim — the wall; sammarjayam asuh — swept clean; saha — together; krishnena — with Krishna; sat-gunah — the virtuous; evam-prakaram — in this manner; nrihareh — of Nrihari; shiksham — instruction; shata-sahasrashah — by hundreds of thousands.

4these virtuous men swept the wall clean together with Krishna. In this way Nrihari gave His instruction hundreds of thousands of times:

Verse 5

भगवान्स्वात्मतन्त्रोऽपि कारुण्येनाभ्यशिक्षयत्।
श्रीमान्गौरचन्द्रदेवो जगतां कारणं परम्॥५॥

bhagavānsvātmatantro'pi kāruṇyenābhyaśikṣayat|
śrīmāngauracandradevo jagatāṁ kāraṇaṁ param||5||

bhagavan — Bhagavan; sva-atma-tantrah — dependent on Himself alone; api — although; karunyena — out of compassion; abhyashikshayat — taught; shriman — the glorious; gaurachandra-devah — Lord Gaurachandra; jagatam — of the worlds; karanam — the cause; param — supreme.

5though Bhagavan depends on no one but Himself, the glorious Lord Gaurachandra, the supreme cause of the worlds, taught out of compassion.

Verse 6

अथ काले व्रजन्तं तं पथि दृष्ट्वा जनार्दनम्।
कश्चित्कुष्ठी नमस्कृत्य विनयानतकन्धरः॥६॥

atha kāle vrajantaṁ taṁ pathi dṛṣṭvā janārdanam|
kaścitkuṣṭhī namaskṛtya vinayānatakandharaḥ||6||

atha — then; kale — in time; vrajantam — walking; tam — that; pathi — on the road; drishtva — seeing; janardanam — Janardana; kashchit — a certain; kushthi — leper; namaskritya — bowing down; vinaya-anata-kandharah — his neck humbly bent.

6One day, seeing Janardana walking along the road, a certain leper bowed down to Him, his neck humbly bent,

Verse 7

उवाच भगवन्सर्वे वदन्ति त्वां सनातनम्।
पुरुषं देवदेवेशं मां समुद्धर पापिनम्॥७॥

uvāca bhagavansarve vadanti tvāṁ sanātanam|
puruṣaṁ devadeveśaṁ māṁ samuddhara pāpinam||7||

uvacha — said; bhagavan — O Bhagavan; sarve — all; vadanti — call; tvam — You; sanatanam — eternal; purusham — Person; deva-deva-isham — Lord of the lords of the gods; mam — me; samuddhara — deliver; papinam — sinful.

7and said: "Bhagavan, everyone calls You the eternal Person, the Lord of the lords of the gods. Deliver me, a sinner!

Verse 8

त्राहि मां दुःसहान्नाथ कुष्ठरोगात्सुदारुणात्।
तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवान्क्रुद्धः शोणपद्मविलोचनः॥८॥

trāhi māṁ duḥsahānnātha kuṣṭharogātsudāruṇāt|
tacchrutvā bhagavānkruddhaḥ śoṇapadmavilocanaḥ||8||

trahi — protect; mam — me; duhsahat — from the unbearable; natha — O Lord; kushtha-rogat — from the disease of leprosy; su-darunat — from the terrible; tat — that; shrutva — hearing; bhagavan — Bhagavan; kruddhah — angered; shona-padma-vilochanah — with eyes like red lotuses.

8O Lord, protect me from this terrible, unbearable leprosy!" Hearing this, Bhagavan grew angry, and His eyes became like red lotuses.

Verse 9

उवाच भो दुराचार वैष्णवद्वेषकारक।
श्रीवासपण्डितद्वेषं कृत्वा त्वं हि कथं सुखी॥९॥

uvāca bho durācāra vaiṣṇavadveṣakāraka|
śrīvāsapaṇḍitadveṣaṁ kṛtvā tvaṁ hi kathaṁ sukhī||9||

uvacha — said; bhoh — ho; durachara — O wicked one; vaishnava-dvesha-karaka — O you who bear hatred for Vaishnavas; shrivasa-pandita-dvesham — hatred for Srivasa Pandita; kritva — having shown; tvam — you; hi — indeed; katham — how; sukhi — happy.

9He said: "Wicked man, hater of Vaishnavas! You have shown enmity to Srivasa Pandita — how can you be happy?

Verse 10

अवाच्यवादमुक्त्वा तं निष्टप्तं वैष्णवोत्तमम्।
शतजन्मनि कुष्ठी त्वं विगताङ्गो भविष्यसि॥१०॥

avācyavādamuktvā taṁ niṣṭaptaṁ vaiṣṇavottamam|
śatajanmani kuṣṭhī tvaṁ vigatāṅgo bhaviṣyasi||10||

avachya-vadam — unspeakable words; uktva — having spoken; tam — to that; nishtaptam — pure as refined gold; vaishnava-uttamam — best of Vaishnavas; shata-janmani — for a hundred births; kushthi — a leper; tvam — you; vigata-angah — limbless; bhavishyasi — will become.

10You spoke unspeakable words against that best of Vaishnavas, pure as gold refined in fire; for a hundred births you shall be a leper, wasting limb by limb.

Verse 11

वैष्णवद्वेषकर्तारं नोद्धरामि कदाचन।
बहिःप्राणमिमं देहमन्तःप्राणं च वैष्णवम्॥११॥

vaiṣṇavadveṣakartāraṁ noddharāmi kadācana|
bahiḥprāṇamimaṁ dehamantaḥprāṇaṁ ca vaiṣṇavam||11||

vaishnava-dvesha-kartaram — one who hates Vaishnavas; na — not; uddharami — I deliver; kadachana — ever; bahih-pranam — the outer life; imam — this; deham — body; antah-pranam — the inner life; cha — and; vaishnavam — the Vaishnava.

11One who hates the Vaishnavas I never deliver. This body is My outer life; the Vaishnava is My inner life.

Verse 12

तं द्विषन्ति महामोहात्पतन्ति निरयेऽशुचौ।
वैष्णवेषु नता ये च मां द्विषन्ति कथञ्चन॥१२॥

taṁ dviṣanti mahāmohātpatanti niraye'śucau|
vaiṣṇaveṣu natā ye ca māṁ dviṣanti kathañcana||12||

tam — him; dvishanti — hate; maha-mohat — out of great delusion; patanti — fall; niraye — into hell; ashuchau — impure; vaishnaveshu — before Vaishnavas; natah — bowed; ye — who; cha — but; mam — Me; dvishanti — hate; kathanchana — in any way.

12Those who out of great delusion hate the Vaishnava fall into an unclean hell. But those who bow before the Vaishnavas and yet in some way bear enmity to Me —

Verse 13

तानुद्धरिष्ये सर्वत्र महापातकसञ्चयात्।
एवमुक्त्वा ययौ देवः श्रीवासस्यालये शुभे॥१३॥

tānuddhariṣye sarvatra mahāpātakasañcayāt|
evamuktvā yayau devaḥ śrīvāsasyālaye śubhe||13||

tan — them; uddharishye — I shall deliver; sarvatra — everywhere; maha-pataka-sanchayat — from a heap of great sins; evam — thus; uktva — having said; yayau — went; devah — the Lord; shrivasasya — of Srivasa; alaye — to the house; shubhe — auspicious.

13them I shall deliver, wherever they are, from their heap of great sins." Having said this, the Lord went to Srivasa's blessed house.

Verse 14

उपविश्य सुखं रेमे भगवान्स्वजनैः सह।
श्रीवासपण्डितं प्राह करुणार्द्रो जगद्गुरुः॥१४॥

upaviśya sukhaṁ reme bhagavānsvajanaiḥ saha|
śrīvāsapaṇḍitaṁ prāha karuṇārdro jagadguruḥ||14||

upavishya — sitting down; sukham — happily; reme — enjoyed; bhagavan — Bhagavan; sva-janaih — with His own people; saha — together; shrivasa-panditam — to Srivasa Pandita; praha — said; karuna-ardrah — softened by compassion; jagat-guruh — the teacher of the world.

14There Bhagavan sat down and happily enjoyed the company of His own. Then the Teacher of the world, softened by compassion, said to Srivasa Pandita:

Verse 15

पथि कश्चित्कुष्ठरोगी दुष्टस्त्वदपराधतः।
भुङ्क्ते स नरकं सर्वमुद्धारो नैव दृश्यते॥१५॥

pathi kaścitkuṣṭharogī duṣṭastvadaparādhataḥ|
bhuṅkte sa narakaṁ sarvamuddhāro naiva dṛśyate||15||

pathi — on the road; kashchit — a certain; kushtha-rogi — leper; dushtah — corrupted; tvat-aparadhatah — through offence against you; bhunkte — suffers; sah — he; narakam — hell; sarvam — all; uddharah — deliverance; na eva — not at all; drishyate — is seen.

15"On the road I met a leper, corrupted by an offence against you. He will suffer every hell, and no deliverance is in sight for him."

Verse 16

स प्राह योऽपराधं मे करोति हि समासतः।
उद्धारं कुरु तं देव वरमेतत्सदा मम॥१६॥

sa prāha yo'parādhaṁ me karoti hi samāsataḥ|
uddhāraṁ kuru taṁ deva varametatsadā mama||16||

sah — he (Srivasa); praha — said; yah — whoever; aparadham — offence; me — to me; karoti — commits; hi — indeed; samasatah — in short; uddharam kuru — deliver; tam — him; deva — O Lord; varam — boon; etat — this; sada — always; mama — for me.

16Srivasa replied: "Lord, whoever offends me — in short, deliver him. This is the boon I always ask.

Verse 17

पापपूर्णाञ्जगन्नाथमाधवादीन्समुद्धर।
ओमित्याह स भगवान्सर्वपातकमूलहृत्॥१७॥

pāpapūrṇāñjagannāthamādhavādīnsamuddhara|
omityāha sa bhagavānsarvapātakamūlahṛt||17||

papa-purnan — full of sin; jagannatha-madhava-adin — Jagannatha, Madhava and others; samuddhara — deliver; om — "so be it"; iti — thus; aha — said; sah — He; bhagavan — Bhagavan; sarva-pataka-mula-hrit — who tears out the root of all sins.

17Deliver also Jagannatha, Madhava and the others, full of sin though they are2." "So be it," said Bhagavan, who tears out the root of all sins.

Verse 18

एकदा ब्राह्मणः कश्चिन्नृत्यन्तं पुरुषोत्तमम्।
द्रष्टुं गत्वा न दृष्ट्वा च बहिर्द्वाःस्थेन वारितः॥१८॥

ekadā brāhmaṇaḥ kaścinnṛtyantaṁ puruṣottamam|
draṣṭuṁ gatvā na dṛṣṭvā ca bahirdvāḥsthena vāritaḥ||18||

ekada — once; brahmanah — a brahmana; kashchit — a certain; nrityantam — dancing; purusha-uttamam — Purushottama; drashtum — to see; gatva — having gone; na — not; drishtva — having seen; cha — and; bahih — outside; dvah-sthena — by the doorkeeper; varitah — stopped.

18Once a certain brahmana came to see Purushottama dancing, but did not see Him: the doorkeeper kept him outside.

Verse 19

रुष्टः परदिने दृष्ट्वा गङ्गातीरे जगद्गुरुम्।
सुदुर्मुखो रुषित्वा तं शापं दास्यन्नुवाच ह॥१९॥

ruṣṭaḥ paradine dṛṣṭvā gaṅgātīre jagadgurum|
sudurmukho ruṣitvā taṁ śāpaṁ dāsyannuvāca ha||19||

rushtah — angered; para-dine — on the next day; drishtva — seeing; ganga-tire — on the bank of the Ganga; jagat-gurum — the teacher of the world; su-durmukhah — foul-mouthed; rushitva — flaring up; tam — at Him; shapam — a curse; dasyan — about to give; uvacha ha — said.

19Angered, he saw the Teacher of the world the next day on the bank of the Ganga and, foul-mouthed and flaring up, spoke out to curse Him.

Verse 20

यज्ञोपवीतं वक्षःस्थं छित्त्वा शापं ददौ क्रुधा।
यस्मात्त्वन्नृत्यसमये तत्र गच्छन्निवारितः॥२०॥

yajñopavītaṁ vakṣaḥsthaṁ chittvā śāpaṁ dadau krudhā|
yasmāttvannṛtyasamaye tatra gacchannivāritaḥ||20||

yajna-upavitam — the sacred thread; vakshah-stham — lying on his chest; chhittva — breaking; shapam — a curse; dadau — gave; krudha — in anger; yasmat — since; tvat-nritya-samaye — at the time of Your dancing; tatra — there; gachchhan — going; nivaritah — was stopped.

20Breaking the sacred thread upon his chest, he cursed Him in his wrath: "Since, when I went there during Your dancing, I was stopped

Verse 21

द्वाःस्थेन ते ततोऽद्य त्वं संसाराद्बहिराव्रज।
तच्छ्रुत्वा ब्राह्मणवचो मुमोद भगवान्परः॥२१॥

dvāḥsthena te tato'dya tvaṁ saṁsārādbahirāvraja|
tacchrutvā brāhmaṇavaco mumoda bhagavānparaḥ||21||

dvah-sthena — by the doorkeeper; te — Your; tatah — therefore; adya — now; tvam — You; samsarat — from worldly (household) life; bahih — out; avraja — go; tat — that; shrutva — hearing; brahmana-vachah — the brahmana's word; mumoda — rejoiced; bhagavan — Bhagavan; parah — the Supreme.

21by Your doorkeeper, go now — out of worldly life!" Hearing the brahmana's words, the Supreme Bhagavan rejoiced:

Verse 22

क्रुद्धब्राह्मणशापो वै वर एवाभवन्मम।
उद्धरामि जनान्सर्वान्सन्न्यासाश्रममाश्रितः॥२२॥

kruddhabrāhmaṇaśāpo vai vara evābhavanmama|
uddharāmi janānsarvānsannyāsāśramamāśritaḥ||22||

kruddha-brahmana-shapah — the curse of the angry brahmana; vai — truly; varah — a boon; eva — indeed; abhavat — has become; mama — for Me; uddharami — I shall deliver; janan — people; sarvan — all; sannyasa-ashramam — the order of sannyasa; ashritah — having taken.

22"The curse of an angry brahmana has become a boon for Me! Taking the order of sannyasa, I shall deliver all people."

Verse 23

इति श्रुत्वा हरेः शापं श्रद्धया परया सह।
ब्रह्मशापाद्विमुच्येत नवं सुखमवाप्नुयात्॥२३॥

iti śrutvā hareḥ śāpaṁ śraddhayā parayā saha|
brahmaśāpādvimucyeta navaṁ sukhamavāpnuyāt||23||

iti — thus; shrutva — hearing; hareh — of Hari; shapam — about the curse; shraddhaya — faith; paraya — supreme; saha — with; brahma-shapat — from a brahmana's curse; vimuchyeta — will be freed; navam — new; sukham — happiness; avapnuyat — will obtain.

23Whoever hears thus, with supreme faith, of the curse laid on Hari will be freed from a brahmana's curse and will find new happiness.

Thus ends the thirteenth sarga, "The Brahmana's Curse as a Boon" (Brahma-shapa-vara), of the second prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Haddipa (Bengali hadi) — a sweeper, a man of the lowest caste who removes refuse. The great devotees gladly take on the humblest service of Krishna.
  2. Jagannatha and Madhava are the brothers Jagai and Madhai, notorious sinners of Navadvipa, later delivered by the Lord and Nityananda.
